what: heart rate variability during sleep time
title: Functionality of the fitbitViz R package
text: Heart Rate Variability (HRV) intraday data single date. HRV data applies specifically user’s “main sleep”, longest single period time asleep given date. measures HRV rate various times returns Root Mean Square Successive Differences (rmssd), Low Frequency (LF), High Frequency (HF), Coverage data given measurement. Rmssd measures short-term variability heart rate asleep. LF HF capture power interbeat interval fluctuations within either high frequency low frequency bands. Finally, coverage refers data completeness terms number interbeat intervals. fitbit_data_type_by_date() function allows user also compute ‘spo2’ (Blood Oxygen Saturation), ‘br’ (Breathing Rate), ‘temp’ (Temperature) ‘cardioscore’ (Cardio Fitness Score VO2 Max) adjusting type parameter.
code: # ....................... # heart rate variability # .......................  hrt_rt_var <- fitbitViz::fitbit_data_type_by_date(   data = heart_dat,   type = "hrv",   plot = TRUE )

title: Functionality of the fitbitViz R package
text: sleep time series visualization similar Fitbit Mobile Visualization x-axis shows specified user sleep time interval whereas y-axis shows sleep Levels (wake, rem, light, deep). Lower levels like deep sleep appear dark blue whereas higher levels like wake appear light blue,
code: # ....................... # sleep data time series # .......................  sleep_ts <- fitbitViz::sleep_time_series(   sleep_data_list = sleep_ts,   ggplot_color_palette = "ggsci::blue_material",   ggplot_ncol = 2,   ggplot_nrow = 4,   verbose = VERBOSE ) sleep_ts$plt_lev_segments

title: Functionality of the fitbitViz R package
text: make use GPS data Fitbit Application, export .tcx file desired activity Fitbit website app pass path GPS_TCX_data(),   following Leaflet Point Coordinates show outdoor activity 11th week 2021 (legend shows elevation route),
code: # .................................................... # return the gps-tcx data.table from an exported .tcx file # ....................................................  res_tcx <- fitbitViz::GPS_TCX_data(   tcx_file = "/path/to/activity.tcx",   time_zone = "Europe/Athens",   verbose = VERBOSE ) # res_tcx # ................................ # Create the Leaflet / LeafGL Map # ................................  res_lft <- fitbitViz::leafGL_point_coords(   dat_gps_tcx = res_tcx,   color_points_column = "AltitudeMeters",   provider = leaflet::providers$Esri.WorldImagery,   option_viewer = rstudioapi::viewer,   CRS = 4326 ) res_lft

title: Functionality of the fitbitViz R package
text: Another option package plot route 3-dimensional space. purpose ’ll use rayshader package, internally uses rgl (OpenGL). First, extend boundaries route approximately 1.000 thousand meters (adjust value depending area interest),   extended area download Copernicus Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data. Copernicus elevation data come either 30 90 meter resolution. pick 30 meter resolution product route. CopernicusDEM R package, make sure installed configured awscli Operating System Requirement intend download reproduce next 3-dimensional map using elevation data,   GPS route use ascending & descending route therefore can convert GPS (TCX) data spatial LINESTRING using maximum altitude split point route visualize ascending route blue descending red (also alternative specify split point based time using time_split_asc_desc parameter),   create ‘elevation_sample_points’ data.table parameter 3-dim plot based min., middle max. altitude previously computed ‘res_tcx’ data,   finally visualize 3-dimensional Rayshader Map,     output map observe 3 specified elevation vertical lines (including altitude values meters) blue color ascending route red color descending route
code: # ................................................... # compute the sf-object buffer and the raster-extend  (1000 meters buffer) # ...................................................  sf_rst_ext <- fitbitViz::extend_AOI_buffer(   dat_gps_tcx = res_tcx,   buffer_in_meters = 1000,   CRS = 4326,   verbose = VERBOSE ) # sf_rst_ext # .................................................................. # Download the Copernicus DEM 30m elevation data # there is also the option to download the DEM 90m elevation data # which is of lower resolution but the image size is smaller which # means faster download # ..................................................................  dem_dir <- tempdir() # dem_dir  dem30 <- CopernicusDEM::aoi_geom_save_tif_matches(   sf_or_file = sf_rst_ext$sfc_obj,   dir_save_tifs = dem_dir,   resolution = 30,   crs_value = 4326,   threads = parallel::detectCores(),   verbose = VERBOSE )  TIF <- list.files(dem_dir, pattern = ".tif", full.names = T) # TIF  if (length(TIF) > 1) {   # ....................................................   # create a .VRT file if I have more than 1 .tif files   # ....................................................    file_out <- file.path(dem_dir, "VRT_mosaic_FILE.vrt")    vrt_dem30 <- CopernicusDEM::create_VRT_from_dir(     dir_tifs = dem_dir,     output_path_VRT = file_out,     verbose = VERBOSE   ) }  if (length(TIF) == 1) {   # ..................................................   # if I have a single .tif file keep the first index   # ..................................................    file_out <- TIF[1] }  # ....................................... # crop the elevation DEM based on the # coordinates extent of the GPS-CTX data # .......................................  raysh_rst <- fitbitViz::crop_DEM(   tif_or_vrt_dem_file = file_out,   sf_buffer_obj = sf_rst_ext$sfc_obj,   verbose = VERBOSE ) # terra::plot(raysh_rst) linestring_dat <- fitbitViz::gps_lat_lon_to_LINESTRING(   dat_gps_tcx = res_tcx,   CRS = 4326,   time_split_asc_desc = NULL,   verbose = VERBOSE ) idx_3m <- c(   which.min(res_tcx$AltitudeMeters),   as.integer(length(res_tcx$AltitudeMeters) / 2),   which.max(res_tcx$AltitudeMeters) )  cols_3m <- c("latitude", "longitude", "AltitudeMeters") dat_3m <- res_tcx[idx_3m, ..cols_3m] # ..................................................... # Conversion of the 'SpatRaster' to a raster object # because the 'rayshader' package accepts only rasters # .....................................................  rst_obj <- raster::raster(raysh_rst) raster::projection(rst_obj) <- terra::crs(raysh_rst, proj = TRUE)   snapshot_rayshader_path <- file.path(tempdir(), "rayshader_img.png")  rgl::open3d(useNULL = TRUE) # this removes the second rgl-popup-window  fitbitViz::rayshader_3d_DEM(   rst_buf = rst_obj,   rst_ext = sf_rst_ext$raster_obj_extent,   linestring_ASC_DESC = linestring_dat,   elevation_sample_points = dat_3m,   zoom = 0.3,   windowsize = c(1000, 800),   add_shadow_rescale_original = FALSE,   verbose = TRUE )  rgl::rgl.snapshot(snapshot_rayshader_path) rgl::par3d(mouseMode = "trackball") # options: c("trackball", "polar", "zoom", "selecting") rgl::rglwidget()

title: Process pre-downloaded Fitbit data for Blood Oxygen Saturation, Heart Rate Variability, Breathing Rate, Temperature and Cardio Fitness Score (or VO2 Max) by Date — fitbit_data_type_by_date
text: 'spo2' (Blood Oxygen Saturation) endpoint returns SpO2 intraday data single date. SpO2 applies specifically user's "main sleep", longest single period time asleep given date. Spo2 values calculated 5-minute exponentially-moving average 'hrv' (Heart Rate Variability) endpoint returns Heart Rate Variability (HRV) intraday data single date. HRV data applies specifically user's "main sleep", longest single period time asleep given date. measures HRV rate various times returns Root Mean Square Successive Differences (rmssd), Low Frequency (LF), High Frequency (HF), Coverage data given measurement. Rmssd measures short-term variability heart rate asleep. LF HF capture power interbeat interval fluctuations within either high frequency low frequency bands. Finally, coverage refers data completeness terms number interbeat intervals 'br' (Breathing Rate) endpoint returns intraday breathing rate data specified date. measures average breathing rate throughout day categories breathing rate sleep stage. Sleep stages vary light sleep, deep sleep, REM sleep, full sleep 'temp' (Temperature) endpoint returns Temperature (Skin) data single date. returns value dates Fitbit device able record Temperature (skin) data. Temperature (Skin) data applies specifically user's "main sleep", longest single period time asleep given date 'cardioscore' (Cardio Fitness Score VO2 Max) Cardio Fitness Score (also known VO2 Max) endpoints used querying maximum optimum rate user's heart, lungs, muscles can effectively use oxygen exercise 'type' parameter one 'spo2' 'hrv' 'plot' parameter set TRUE results appear line plot. case 'hrv' multiplot following variables displayed: 'rmssd' Root Mean Square Successive Differences (RMSSD) heart beats. measures short-term variability user's heart rate milliseconds (ms) 'coverage' Data completeness terms number interbeat intervals 'hf' power interbeat interval fluctuations within high frequency band (0.15 Hz - 0.4 Hz) 'lf' power interbeat interval fluctuations within low frequency band (0.04 Hz - 0.15 Hz)

title: Rayshader 3-dimensional using the Copernicus DEM elevation data — rayshader_3d_DEM
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{  require(fitbitViz)  # export the TCX file from the Fitbit website or app for the desired activity  res_tcx <- GPS_TCX_data(   tcx_file = "/path/to/activity.tcx",   time_zone = "Europe/Athens",   verbose = TRUE ) str(res_tcx)  # .................................................... # then compute the sf-object buffer and raster-extend # ....................................................  sf_rst_ext <- extend_AOI_buffer(   dat_gps_tcx = res_tcx,   buffer_in_meters = 1000,   CRS = 4326,   verbose = TRUE ) sf_rst_ext  # ............................................................... # Download the Copernicus DEM 30m elevation data because it has # a better resolution, it takes a bit longer to download because # the .tif file size is bigger # ...............................................................  dem_dir <- tempdir() # dem_dir  dem30 <- CopernicusDEM::aoi_geom_save_tif_matches(   sf_or_file = sf_rst_ext$sfc_obj,   dir_save_tifs = dem_dir,   resolution = 30,   crs_value = 4326,   threads = parallel::detectCores(),   verbose = TRUE )  TIF <- list.files(dem_dir, pattern = ".tif", full.names = T) # TIF  if (length(TIF) > 1) {   # ....................................................   # create a .VRT file if I have more than 1 .tif files   # ....................................................    file_out <- file.path(dem_dir, "VRT_mosaic_FILE.vrt")    vrt_dem30 <- create_VRT_from_dir(     dir_tifs = dem_dir,     output_path_VRT = file_out,     verbose = TRUE   ) }  if (length(TIF) == 1) {   # ..................................................   # if I have a single .tif file keep the first index   # ..................................................    file_out <- TIF[1] }  raysh_rst <- crop_DEM(   tif_or_vrt_dem_file = file_out,   sf_buffer_obj = sf_rst_ext$sfc_obj,   verbose = TRUE )  # terra::plot(raysh_rst)   # ................................................................ # create the 'elevation_sample_points' data.table parameter based # on the min., middle  and max. altitude of the 'res_tcx' data # ................................................................  idx_3m <- c(   which.min(res_tcx$AltitudeMeters),   as.integer(length(res_tcx$AltitudeMeters) / 2),   which.max(res_tcx$AltitudeMeters) )  cols_3m <- c("latitude", "longitude", "AltitudeMeters") dat_3m <- res_tcx[idx_3m, ..cols_3m] # dat_3m  # ............................................................... # Split the route in 2 parts based on the maximum altitude value # ...............................................................  linestring_dat <- gps_lat_lon_to_LINESTRING(   dat_gps_tcx = res_tcx,   CRS = 4326,   time_split_asc_desc = NULL,   verbose = TRUE )  # ..................................................... # Conversion of the 'SpatRaster' to a raster object # because the 'rayshader' package accepts only rasters # .....................................................  rst_obj <- raster::raster(raysh_rst) raster::projection(rst_obj) <- terra::crs(raysh_rst, proj = TRUE)   # ..................................... # open the 3-dimensional rayshader map # .....................................  ray_out <- rayshader_3d_DEM(   rst_buf = rst_obj,   rst_ext = sf_rst_ext$raster_obj_extent,   linestring_ASC_DESC = linestring_dat,   elevation_sample_points = dat_3m,   zoom = 0.5,   windowsize = c(1600, 1000),   add_shadow_rescale_original = FALSE,   verbose = TRUE ) } # }

title: fitbitViz 1.0.8
text: Breaking change — Fitbit Web API dependency removed. functions previously required user_id token refactored accept pre-downloaded data directly, eliminating dependency httr, jsonlite, base64enc. change driven recurring Fitbit API policy changes (GitHub issues #4, #5, #7, #8, #11). Removed functions: base_url_request(), refresh_token_app(), extract_LOG_ID() — API-helpers visualization logic. heart_rate_time_series(heart_rate_intraday_list, heart_rate = NULL, ...) — accepts named list intraday data.tables fitbit_data_type_by_date(data, type = 'spo2', ...) — accepts parsed JSON response date/type sleep_single_day(sleep_data, date, ...) — accepts parsed sleep API response sleep_time_series(sleep_data_list, ...) — accepts named list per-date sleep responses GPS_TCX_data(tcx_file, time_zone, ...) — accepts path exported .tcx file Sample data: inst/tests_vignette_rds/ folder ships .RDS files (heart_dat.RDS, sleep_ts.RDS, res_tcx.RDS) illustrate expected input structure refactored function. Users need previous API-based version can install remotes::install_github("mlampros/fitbitViz@v1.0.7") CRAN archive https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/fitbitViz/fitbitViz_1.0.7.tar.gz.
